title: Document the core Mosaic architecture
body:
## Goal

Create a clear, beginner-friendly explanation of the core Project Mosaic architecture.

## Context

Project Mosaic is an experimental game-engine architecture built around composable Blocks, graphs, compilation, and replaceable systems. A new contributor should be able to read the documentation and understand the basic flow without having to inspect the entire repository.

## Tasks

- Explain what a Mosaic Block represents.
- Explain how Blocks are connected into a graph.
- Explain the role of graph compilation.
- Explain the purpose of the intermediate representation (IR).
- Explain how the compiled representation eventually reaches an execution/runtime layer.
- Explain where replaceable systems/backends fit into the architecture.
- Create a simple architecture diagram showing the major stages.

## Expected result

A concise architecture document and/or diagram explaining:

`Blocks → Graph → Validation → Compilation → IR → Execution`

## Notes

This is an architectural experiment. Alternative approaches are welcome. If something in the current design is unclear or inconsistent, document the problem rather than silently assuming an answer.

title: Define the initial Block interface
body:
## Goal

Design the minimal interface required for a Mosaic Block.

## Context

Mosaic is based around composable Blocks that can be connected into graphs and eventually compiled into an executable representation. The goal is to determine the smallest useful interface without prematurely locking the engine into a large framework.

## Tasks

- Identify the minimum information a Block needs.
- Define how inputs are represented.
- Define how outputs are represented.
- Consider how types should be represented.
- Consider whether Blocks should be stateful or stateless.
- Consider whether Blocks need metadata.
- Create a small C++ prototype of the proposed interface.
- Document the major design decisions.

## Expected result

A proposed/implemented minimal Block interface with a short design document explaining the decisions.

## Notes

This is an architectural experiment. Alternative approaches are welcome.

title: Create a minimal Graph data structure
body:
## Goal

Create a minimal graph representation capable of storing Mosaic Blocks and their connections.

## Context

Mosaic uses graphs to represent relationships between composable Blocks. Before compilation or execution can happen, we need a reliable representation of this graph.

## Tasks

Implement a minimal Graph abstraction that supports:
- Adding Blocks/nodes.
- Removing Blocks/nodes.
- Connecting outputs to inputs.
- Removing connections.
- Looking up nodes.
- Iterating over nodes and connections.
- Basic graph traversal.

## Expected result

A small, self-contained Graph implementation with tests and at least one example (e.g. Input → Transform → Output).

## Notes

This is an architectural experiment. Alternative approaches are welcome. Consider how nodes are identified, how connections are represented, and whether the graph should own its Blocks.

title: Add graph validation
body:
## Goal

Create a validation system that can detect invalid Mosaic graphs before compilation/execution.

## Context

A graph should be validated before it reaches later stages of the pipeline. Validation should catch structural problems early and provide useful diagnostics rather than generic failure messages.

## Tasks

Investigate and implement validation for issues such as:
- Connections referencing nonexistent nodes.
- Missing required inputs.
- Invalid input/output connections.
- Incompatible port types.
- Cycles where cycles are not permitted.

## Expected result

A validation pass that can inspect a graph and return useful diagnostics identifying the problematic parts.

## Notes

This is an architectural experiment. Alternative approaches are welcome. Consider whether cycles are always invalid and how multiple validation errors should be reported.

title: Prototype Graph → IR conversion
body:
## Goal

Create a small prototype that converts a validated Mosaic graph into an intermediate representation (IR).

## Context

One of Mosaic's central ideas is separating the user-facing graph from the representation used for compilation and execution. The IR should provide a cleaner representation for later optimization and scheduling.

## Tasks

- Define a minimal IR representation.
- Define how Blocks map to IR nodes/instructions.
- Define how connections map to IR relationships.
- Implement conversion from a small valid graph into the IR.
- Preserve the information required for later execution.

## Expected result

A minimal working Graph → IR prototype and documentation explaining the chosen representation (e.g., converting Input → Add → Output into LoadInput, Add, StoreOutput instructions).

## Notes

This is an architectural experiment. Alternative approaches are welcome. Consider whether the IR should be graph-based, instruction-based, or hybrid.

title: Prototype dependency-based execution scheduling
body:
## Goal

Create a prototype that determines a valid execution order for dependent Mosaic nodes.

## Context

A Mosaic graph describes relationships between operations, but the runtime eventually needs a scheduled execution order.

## Tasks

- Analyze dependencies between nodes.
- Implement a basic topological scheduling algorithm.
- Detect dependency cycles.
- Produce a deterministic execution order where possible.

## Expected result

A small scheduler that accepts a dependency graph/IR and produces a valid, deterministic execution order.

## Notes

This is an architectural experiment. Alternative approaches are welcome. Consider whether independent nodes should be allowed to execute in parallel and whether scheduling should happen on the Graph or IR.

title: Create a minimal 2D Mosaic example
body:
## Goal

Create a tiny example demonstrating how Mosaic's architecture could be used to represent a simple 2D game/system.

## Context

Mosaic is ultimately intended to support game development, so we need small practical examples that test whether the architecture is actually useful and identify any architectural friction early.

## Tasks

- Define the Blocks required for the example (e.g. Input → Movement → Transform → Render).
- Construct the corresponding graph.
- Validate the graph.
- Demonstrate compilation/IR generation if available.

## Expected result

A small runnable or inspectable example showing how a simple 2D system can be represented using Mosaic.

## Notes

This is an architectural experiment. Alternative approaches are welcome. The goal is NOT to create a complete game, but to expose useful architectural insights.

title: Investigate requirements for a Vulkan backend
body:
## Goal

Investigate what a Vulkan backend would need to look like within Mosaic.

## Context

Mosaic is intended to support replaceable systems/backends. Vulkan is one potential graphics backend, but the engine architecture should avoid becoming tightly coupled to Vulkan-specific concepts.

## Tasks

Research and document:
- What the graphics abstraction should expose.
- Which concepts should remain backend-independent.
- Which concepts necessarily belong to the Vulkan backend.
- How resources, command submission, and synchronization should be represented.

## Expected result

A short technical design/research document describing a possible Vulkan backend architecture.

## Notes

This is an architectural experiment. Alternative approaches are welcome. A conclusion that a particular approach is a bad idea is a valid result.

title: Add tests for core Mosaic architecture
body:
## Goal

Create a collection of small tests/examples that verify Mosaic's core architectural assumptions.

## Context

Because Mosaic is experimental, tests are useful not only for preventing regressions but also for determining whether the architecture behaves as expected.

## Tasks

Create tests for areas such as:
- Block creation and input/output definitions.
- Graph construction, connections, and validation.
- Graph traversal and scheduling.

## Expected result

A small suite of tests that exercise the fundamental Mosaic pipeline and run automatically as part of the normal development workflow.

## Notes

This is an architectural experiment. Alternative approaches are welcome. Tests should be small and easy to understand.

title: Improve developer setup and contribution documentation
body:
## Goal

Make it easy for a new developer to clone Mosaic, build it, understand the repository structure, and make their first contribution.

## Context

We want to minimize onboarding friction so that someone unfamiliar with Mosaic can go from cloning the repository to running tests and contributing changes without needing manual help.

## Tasks

Improve documentation covering:
- Required tools, dependencies, and supported platforms.
- Build instructions and running tests.
- Repository structure and guide on how to add a Block/example.
- Contribution workflow and current limitations.

## Expected result

Updated developer documentation and instructions that guide a new contributor from checkout to first change.

## Notes

This is an architectural experiment. Alternative approaches are welcome. Common setup problems should be documented.
